short: A short, transitional reign that began the practice of choosing an heir by adoption rather than blood.
full:
Nerva, an elderly senator with a long record of loyal service to the Flavians, was proclaimed emperor by the Senate within a day of Domitian's assassination on 18 September 96 CE, chosen precisely because he had no sons who might found a new dynasty. His reign was troubled by an unpaid Praetorian Guard, which briefly besieged the palace in 97 CE and forced him to hand over Domitian's killers.

To secure his position and the succession, Nerva adopted the respected general Trajan as his son and heir that autumn, a choice that satisfied both the army and the Senate. Nerva died on 27 January 98 CE after little more than a year in power, but the precedent he set — selecting the ablest available successor by adoption rather than passing the throne to a blood relative — shaped the next eighty years of stable rule.
